chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, concerning:
The urine of riding animals gets onto the garment, and he disliked it. So I said: Are not their meats halal? He said: “Yes, but it is not from that which Allah has made for eating.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report governs the rest of the reports that contain the command to wash the garment from the urine and dung of these things, for what is meant by them is a kind of karāhah, and he has stated that explicitly as you see.

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: urine; the substance discussed in relation to clothing and purity
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: garment; the clothing affected by the urine
key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: riding animals or beasts; the animals whose urine is being discussed
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: report; the narration used as evidence in legal reconciliation
key_terms.الْكَرَاهَةِ: karāhah; a ruling of dislikedness rather than impurity or prohibition
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine; mentioned again in the legal discussion
key_terms.لِلْأَكْلِ: for eating; indicating what Allah has designated as food

ai.seo_question: Is the urine of halal animals like riding animals najis, and must clothing be washed from it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a garment affected by the urine of riding animals whose meat is halal. The Imam عليهما السلام expresses dislike rather than impurity, and Shaykh al-Ṭūsī states that reports commanding washing in such cases are to be understood as indicating karāhah, not najasah.
